title: Statuspage epoch snapshot and verification instructions - short-form customer update
summary: Concise statuspage update and customer-facing verification/instruction set after an intermittent inference degradation on 2026-05-22. Focused on what happened, immediate mitigations, optional customer verification steps, and how to request replay/evidence packages.
statuspage_update: What happened: Between 2026-05-22 03:12 UTC and 2026-05-22 03:47 UTC we observed a regional inference attenuation affecting a subset of requests in eu-west-1. Some requests experienced increased tokenization latency and occasional truncated structured outputs. Impact: ~0.7% of total requests in the region had either slow responses (>1.5s increase) or structured-output truncation. Scope: Hosted API tenants in eu-west-1 only; dedicated and private deployments unaffected. Current status: The service is fully recovered and routing to standard model variants has resumed. We deployed an emergency kernel rollback and adjusted the KV cache eviction threshold to prevent recurrences during the traffic window. Next update: Final customer postmortem and evidence package availability scheduled by 2026-05-27.
customer_postmortem:
Root cause (summary): A push to a kernel-selection tuning change created a subtle mismatch for long-prefix KV cache eviction under a low-memory pressure corner case. That mismatch caused transient KV lookups to miss and fall back to slower code paths; for some structured-output generation pipelines this manifested as early EOS behavior (truncation). Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-05-22 03:07 UTC: Canary alerts indicate slight latency rise in eu-west-1.
- 2026-05-22 03:12 UTC: Broader rollouts see elevated error rates; automated routing reduced new session placement into the affected pool.
- 2026-05-22 03:20 UTC: Ops routing rules shifted traffic to cold pools; this mitigated most latency but not truncation.
- 2026-05-22 03:33 UTC: Engineering identified kernel-selection change as probable cause and prepared rollback.
- 2026-05-22 03:40 UTC: Emergency rollback and KV threshold change deployed.
- 2026-05-22 03:47 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline; post-deploy validation began.
What we fixed: Rolled back the kernel-selection delta, reinstated previous safe eviction thresholds, and added a fast-path health check to detect KV miss storming. What we will do next:
- short term (<=2 weeks): automated canary checks for KV miss patterns, additional unit tests around prefix-cache eviction, and a staged configuration flag for kernel-selection changes.
- medium term (<=3 months): telemetry improvements for per-tenant KV miss rates, and a chaos-test that simulates low-memory eviction races.
Customer impact and mitigations: We identified tenants that saw either delayed responses or truncated structured outputs. Where possible we reprocessed queued inference work internally and offer an evidence package and optional replay (see below). We are offering a one-time credit for affected request volume; contact CS for account-specific calculation.
Apology and commitment: We regret the disruption. Our goal is predictable inference economics and output quality; we will publish a full technical write-up and a release of the added telemetry within the timeline above.
action_items: For customers who saw data impact: 1) Option to request a replay and evidence package (hash-indexed) via our Customer Ops portal. 2) Option for a manual re-run of affected prompt batches (if they provide the request window and sample ids). 3) If you run deterministic evaluation suites, we recommend re-running them against post-rollback model variants and notifying your Redwood CS contact if you observe regressions. How to request: open ticket referencing INC-4521 and include tenant-id and sample request ids. Deadline for replay requests: 2026-06-10.
verification_instructions: We provide a compact verification kit so clients can confirm whether their requests were affected without sharing full payload data. Steps: 1) Identify your tenant and approximate request window (2026-05-22 03:10-03:50 UTC). 2) From the Customer Ops portal request a verification token for that window (token TTL: 72 hours). 3) Using the token you will receive a compressed manifest listing per-request signatures (HMAC-SHA256) and a small, redacted metadata CSV (timestamps, route, token_count). 4) Locally compute HMACs for your retained request IDs and compare; matches indicate the records are present in our evidence package. 5) If you want a full replay of plaintext inputs, you must submit a replay-consent form (link provided in evidence package). We log replay approvals and require an audit-signature. If you prefer not to submit inputs, the HMAC/manifest is sufficient to claim the credit and for reconciliation.
customer_notes: Short guidance for engineering leads: - Temporarily prefer model variants without length-sensitive structured decoders if you rely on strict EOS semantics until we ship the medium-term fixes. - Enable the 'strict-prefix-cache' guard in your tenant settings (contact CS for assistance) to reduce likelihood of eviction-induced misses. - If you have automated alerting for output truncation, update rules to watch for sudden rises in 'structured_eos_rate' metric. Communication: We will publish the final postmortem on the public statuspage and notify tenants via email. If you need priority assistance or a dedicated technical runbook for replaying sensitive datasets, request a CS engagement and we will queue you into prioritized remediation support.
notes_to_self: Make sure engineering includes the small diagnostic dump (KV miss histograms) in the evidence package. Confirm legal signoff for replay-consent wording. Coordinate credit calculation with finance: use the per-token median cost model rather than peak. Draft final public postmortem by 2026-05-27 and run it by product and infra leads for redaction of any sensitive internals.
footer: Prepared by Customer Success (Ravi Menon). Triage owner: Michael Ortiz. Engineering reviewer: Asha Patel. Draft v0.3 - internal review only.
